Nobody yet knew whether Nella was behind the cattails or away.

Mira and Pip pushed the reed stage onto the pond. It floated proudly, though one corner wiggled like a ticklish duck. Mira draped the lantern ribbon across the stage. The lights blinked on, making the pond look sprinkled with tiny moons.

Tom thumped the kettle-drum. BOOM! Three frogs leaped, one frog applauded, and a lily pad put both hands over its face. “That,” said Tom, “was only my polite finale.”

Pip sent the paper invitation sliding through the cattails, where it landed with a polite little plop.

A hand appeared between the cattails and accepted the invitation. Nella did not step out yet, but one bright eye peeked toward the pond.

The invitation fluttered, the lanterns glowed, and Mira called, “Welcome to the pond concert!” From the cattails came a pleased rustle.

Tom struck the finale. BOOM-BOOM-BOOM! Frogs cheered, lily pads bounced, and Tom grinned so widely that his ears nearly became parentheses.

The frogs presented Tom with the Golden Tadpole Spoon. He lifted it high; it wobbled in the moonlight like a very tiny trophy moon.

The drum’s last boom rolled away, and Tom tucked the wobbling spoon beside his heart.

Pip pressed one toe to the mud and listened. Behind the cattails, he discovered that Nella’s hearing was keen. “Then even a whisper can be a concert,” he said.

“I want to play the moon-song for Nella,” Pip told Tom. “It has three soft notes and one enormous feeling.” Tom looked at the drum, which suddenly seemed very enormous too.

Pip leaned toward Tom. “Nella can hear keenly,” he whispered. Tom’s drumstick froze halfway to the sky. “Keenly?”

Pip sent the paper invitation sliding through the cattails, where it landed with a polite little plop. Mira and Pip pushed the reed stage onto the pond. It floated proudly, though one corner wiggled like a ticklish duck.

Tom looked at Pip, then at the drum. “All right,” he said. “Your moon-song first. I’ll make my finale small enough to fit in a frog’s pocket.” Pip beamed; Tom’s drumstick gave a brave little salute.

Pip sang his moon-song on the floating stage. The notes curled over the water, and even the lantern ribbon seemed to lean closer.

A hand appeared between the cattails and accepted the invitation. Nella did not step out yet, but one bright eye peeked toward the pond.

Mira draped the lantern ribbon across the stage. The lights blinked on, making the pond look sprinkled with tiny moons. The invitation fluttered, the lanterns glowed, and Mira called, “Welcome to the pond concert!” From the cattails came a pleased rustle.

Pip’s moon-song floated first. Then Tom added a playful ripple—tap, tap, wobble, BOOM! The frogs cheered for both sounds, and the stage bobbed like it was laughing.

For the concert’s two-part sparkle, the frogs gave Tom the Golden Tadpole Spoon. He shared its shine with Pip by tilting it between them.

The cheers faded into chuckles as the reed stage settled beneath its lanterns.
